priorInvolvementDisclosure: I authored the frozen Claude v14 REJECT (27a42422). Two of the three repairs v15 claims trace to me: CLAUDE-HEA14-S1 was my finding, and HAE14-CX-02 is Codex's escalation of CLAUDE-HEA14-A1, an advisory I explicitly declined to raise as blocking. The second is the sharper lesson and I recorded it in my stub before analysis. My severity calls in this lineage have now been under-called twice, at v9 where I graded the D-032 whole-file pin an advisory and Codex found it misattributed to the wrong decision, and at v14 where I graded the advisory omission non-blocking and Codex made it a finding that produced a repair. I therefore treated my own severity instinct as the weak instrument this round and tested completeness by enumeration instead: I extracted every finding id from all twelve pinned verdict files for v9 through v14 and diffed those sets against the register, rather than sampling or reading for intent.

shouldFix.title: The advisory-registration repair is applied to v9-v13 but not to the v14 round that produced it, so HAE14-CX-02 is recorded REPAIRED while its own defect persists for the current generation
evidence: The artifact affirmatively claims advisory coverage rather than narrowing away from it. honestyRepairsKeyRule now reads in part: 'Every finding id in predecessorVerdictFindings for v8 onward, including BLOCKER and ADVISORY, MUST appear in honestyRepairsFromVN or in that generation's register findings[].' Codex's frozen requiredRepair offered the alternative of narrowing to an actionable-only register with a separate advisory lineage; v15 did not take it, and broadened the rule to name ADVISORY instead.

The intended shape is demonstrated for five consecutive rounds. Eleven advisory ids are registered with disposition ADVISORY-NON-BLOCKING: CLAUDE-HEA9-A1/A2/A3, CLAUDE-HEA11-A1/A2, HAE11-ADV-01/02, HAE12-ADV-01, CLAUDE-HEA13-A1/A2 and HAE13-ADV-01. I confirmed the register is complete against the frozen files for every one of v9, v10, v11, v12 and v13, both reviewers.

The v14 round departs from that shape. Diffing the register against the two frozen v14 verdicts the dispatch pins: the Claude v14 file carries CLAUDE-HEA14-S1 and CLAUDE-HEA14-A1, and the register records only CLAUDE-HEA14-S1; the Codex v14 file carries HAE14-CX-01, HAE14-CX-02, HAE14-ADV-01, HAE14-ADV-02 and HAE14-ADV-03, and the register records only the two CX ids. Four advisory ids are omitted: CLAUDE-HEA14-A1, HAE14-ADV-01, HAE14-ADV-02, HAE14-ADV-03.

That is the same defect Codex raised, one generation later and with a smaller count. HAE14-CX-02's frozen title is 'The governing per-finding register omits eleven frozen advisory findings without defining an advisory exclusion'. v15 registers those eleven and omits four new ones created by the very review round it is answering.

The register nonetheless records the finding as fully discharged. predecessorVerdictFindings.v14.codex records HAE14-CX-02 with disposition REPAIRED and at 'eleven advisory ids registered with ADVISORY-NON-BLOCKING', and honestyRepairsFromV14[2] names exactly those eleven. Neither notes that the current round's advisories are outstanding.

The omitted ids are substantively live, not spurious. HAE14-ADV-01, ADV-02 and ADV-03 are Codex's independent restatements of the three subjects I raised as CLAUDE-HEA11-A1/A2 and CLAUDE-HEA13-A1/A2 and declined to escalate: FC-SUBTYPE-CLASS still exercises no CA-3 row, destinations.actionSubtype still mixes record and serialized class vocabulary in one requiredness clause, and coveredActs retains non-discriminator case variants. All three remain unaddressed in the v15 text.
shouldFix.impact: A reader applying the artifact's own GOVERNING rule to the v14 round gets an incomplete finding set, which is precisely the property HAE14-CX-02 was raised to establish and which the register exists to guarantee. Worse, the register asserts REPAIRED for that finding, so the artifact reports the gap closed while carrying it. Because each successor is reviewed against the accumulated finding set, an advisory that never enters the register at the round it was raised has no mechanism to enter later, which is how the three substantive advisory subjects above have now survived unaddressed from v11 to v15 while being re-raised under fresh ids each generation.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Register the four omitted v14 advisory ids with explicit dispositions in the same ADVISORY-NON-BLOCKING form already used for the other eleven, and amend the honestyRepairsFromV14 entry and the v14 register disposition for HAE14-CX-02 so neither claims a completeness the record does not have. Then state in honestyRepairsKeyRule that the register for round N is complete against both frozen verdicts of round N at the time the successor is authored, so the obligation attaches to the current round rather than only to rounds already closed. If instead an actionable-only register is intended, take Codex's other branch explicitly: narrow the rule, drop the eleven advisory registrations or move them to a separate advisory lineage, and stop claiming per-finding coverage.

advisories.title: Three substantive advisory subjects remain unaddressed from v11 through v15 under three successive id sets
advisories.observation: FC-SUBTYPE-CLASS still exercises no CA-3 row despite CA-3 carrying the largest subtype domain including the deferred KEYCHAIN; destinations.actionSubtype still reads 'Required for CA-1, CA-3, CA-4-HOST' followed by the fully serialized restatement 'on CA-1/CA-3/CA-4'; and coveredActs still keys the host classes as CA-1-host-head and CA-4-host against the record vocabulary CA-1-HOST-HEAD and CA-4-HOST. I raised these as CLAUDE-HEA11-A1/A2 and CLAUDE-HEA13-A1/A2, and Codex raised them independently as HAE14-ADV-01/02/03.
advisories.whyNotShouldFix: Each is genuinely non-blocking on its own terms and I have twice declined to escalate them; doing so now, in the round where their registration is already the subject of CLAUDE-HEA15-S1, would double-count the same underlying fact. Recorded so the subjects survive in this verdict independently of whether the register picks up their ids.
advisories.suggestedDisposition: Optional and not a condition of adoption. Adding one CA-3 accept row and one CA-3 cross-class refuse row would close the first at negligible cost.

verdictBasis: The dispatch permits ACCEPT only at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. This review returns 0 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX, so the verdict is REJECT. Two of the three claimed repairs are complete and verified mechanically: my own CLAUDE-HEA14-S1 is discharged on the branch I offered, with the cross-check that produced it now returning zero gaps, and Codex's HAE14-CX-01 is discharged on all three named elements including a relabel fixture built from two individually valid objects, which is the hard version of that test. Custody is clean on every pin, all 46 recorded inputs reproduce, the D-032 section reproduces, mapping totality and every prior-generation repair are intact, and the leaf-path diff shows zero removals. The third repair is where it stops. HAE14-CX-02 asked that the register stop omitting advisory findings; v15 registers the eleven that existed when the finding was written, broadens the governing rule to name ADVISORY rather than taking Codex's offered narrowing, and then omits all four advisories produced by the v14 round itself, while recording that finding as REPAIRED. That is the same defect one generation later, and the three subjects behind the omitted Codex ids have now gone unaddressed from v11 to v15 under three successive id sets, which is what the omission costs in practice. Four register entries and a corrected disposition close it.
